instructions:
Webcite reads documents and checks claims against sources. Use it to: (1) convert a PDF, scan, spreadsheet or office file to Markdown with page and sheet locations (upload_file or upload_url, then extract_document); (2) verify one factual claim against web sources with citations and a verdict (verify_claim); (3) check that quotes appear in their sources (verify_batch); (4) fact-check every claim in a document with a coverage report (review_document, then get_document_review_job and get_document_review); (5) extract and cross-check figures (extract_figures, analyze_conflicts); (6) find sources without a verdict (search_sources). webcite_guide with workflow=choose lists each workflow with inputs and cost.

To audit an entire uploaded document or every figure on a slide, use review_document with its existing asset_id, then poll get_document_review_job. Do not substitute a few verify_claim calls for full coverage. Only claim full coverage when the saved review reports coverage_complete=true and no pending claims.
Reuse returned extraction structuredContent; each repeated extract call is charged again.

Workflows:
1) Plain fact → verify_claim({ claim })
2) Quote in a document → upload_file → extract_document → get_source_preview → verify_batch
3) Figures / conflicts → extract_document first; analyze_document accepts PDF, spreadsheet and JPEG/PNG/WebP. Image figures are OCR/model reads and need source review. extract_figures finds recognized metrics only; zero metrics is not a full numeric audit.
4) Full document fact-check → webcite_guide({ workflow: 'document_review' }); upload original bytes only if needed, then review_document with stable thread_id (no mandatory balance or extraction preflight), get_document_review_job until terminal, then get_document_review for saved results and coverage. No fixed claim count. Preserve completed results and unchecked source spans on errors or credit exhaustion.
5) Find the original source behind an image or slide → webcite_guide({ workflow: 'source_trace' }); extract_document, search_sources using exact table values and units, then get_source_preview on candidate URLs. Use verify_claim with confirmed source_urls for claim truth. ask_document is numerical Q&A over supplied text, not an external-source finder.

Do not call context workflow/eval tools unless WEBCITE_MCP_PROFILE=full and the user asks.
Never invent citation URLs. Prefer get_source_preview to show evidence.
Profiles default to public; WEBCITE_MCP_PROFILE=core|docs|research|full changes local discovery.

Reporting saved results: Compact fields omitted are unknown, not absent. Report known material_claims (physical rows excluding duplicates), total_claims (all physical rows), duplicate_claims and non_factual_claims separately. Material counts can include non-factual rows and do not imply every row is factual. A duplicate display alias can have a different id; original_claim_id is its stored original identity and duplicate_of_id identifies the canonical assertion. Display aliases do not change stored IDs, citations or paid operations. Report pending, failed, rejected and uncovered counts separately. pending_claims is unfinished work and includes failed_claims; failed is a subset, never add it again to a total. Counts do not establish attempt history; without attempt data, do not call unfinished rows never attempted. A provider access error does not rule out incomplete extraction or source coverage. Null or missing counts are unknown, never zero. Do not group unknown rejected or uncovered counts with known zero pending or failed counts. A completed job means processing finished; it does not prove complete source coverage. For a queued or running review, obey poll_after_ms with waits of at most 30 seconds. Never multiply remaining claims by per-claim latency into a long blind sleep. Stop polling immediately on a terminal status and report failed or interrupted work. Do not infer source weighting, prioritization or analysis absence from omissions. Fetch verbose evidence details only when that specific audit requires them.

tools.name: webcite_guide
tools.title: Choose a Webcite workflow
tools.description: Lists Webcite workflows (parse a document, verify a claim, check quotes, review a whole document, check figures, trace a source) with inputs, order and cost. workflow=choose lists the options; workflow=source_trace covers finding the original source of a screenshot or slide; workflow=document_review covers checking every claim in an uploaded file; workflow=billing covers plan allocations and prices. Returns Markdown only, with no structuredContent. Costs 0 credits. Related: get_credit_balance reads the balance of this account rather than plan prices.

workflow.description: Which workflow to explain. Default choose lists options; billing is the account and billing reference; folders is the folder hierarchy HTTP API.

question.description: Optional user question or claim to embed in examples

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.title: Get credit balance
tools.description: Read the authenticated account credit balance for an explicit balance question or an unresolved credit refusal. A routine document review does not require this call; use inline credit_usage from normal responses. Costs 0 credits. Returns how many credits are left (remaining), used and total; no billing change is made. Related: webcite_guide with workflow=billing explains plan allocations and prices rather than this account's balance.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.title: Verify a claim against sources
tools.description:
Fact-check one claim against web sources: returns citations, a stance for each source (supports/contradicts/neutral) and a verdict.

Use this when you need to:
- Fact-check one specific claim (whole-document review is a separate tool, review_document)
- Find sources that support or contradict a statement
- Check whether a statement is true, with a confidence score

Related: verify_claim_stream adds the intermediate stream events; verify_batch matches quotes to sources you supply, with no verdict; verify_numeric_claim covers arithmetic on retained figures; search_sources skips stance and verdict.

Credits: 2-4 depending on options (search: 2, +stance: 1, +verdict: 1)

idempotency_key.description: Reuse the same key and arguments for a JSON verify retry. Changed arguments are rejected. If settlement is unresolved, the API returns an error and does not charge again.

claim.description: The factual claim to verify (e.g., "The Eiffel Tower is 330 meters tall")

source_urls.description: Up to five public HTTPS source URLs, including readable PDFs, to read directly. Pass user-provided official reports here rather than relying on search.

filters.description: Optional source constraints. A source whose required metadata is unknown does not match.

source_type.description: Allowed source types (1 to 20), e.g. "Government Document", "Dataset", "Journal", "Report".

is_primary_source.description: true: primary sources only; false: non-primary only.

official_country.description: Two-letter lower-case country code, e.g. "us", for official sources of that country.

to.description: Latest year (4 digits), not before from.

domain.description: Only these domains and their subdomains (1 to 20).

exclude_domain.description: Never these domains, their subdomains or redirects into them (1 to 20).

thread_id.description: Thread ID to group related verifications in a session. Pass the same thread_id to continue a conversation.

include_stance.description: Include stance analysis (supports/contradicts) for each source. Adds 1 credit. Default: true

include_verdict.description: Generate an overall verdict with confidence score. Adds 1 credit. Default: true

decompose_claim.description: Break complex claims into sub-claims and verify each independently. Useful for multi-part claims.

tools.name: search_sources
tools.title: Search for sources
tools.description:
Search the web for sources on a query and return citations, without stance or verdict.

Use this when you need to:
- Find sources or references to cite on a topic quickly
- Find official or primary sources, using filters for country, domain and year
- Trace an original report from a screenshot or slide using its distinctive values, units and years; returns candidate URLs
- Get raw search results for further analysis
- Save credits by skipping analysis

Related: verify_claim also searches but judges each source and returns a verdict on the claim; get_source_preview opens one known source at its quoted passage.

Credits: 2 (search only)

query.description: Search query or claim to find sources for. For source tracing, include the exact values, units and years.

filters.description: Optional source constraints. A source whose required metadata is unknown does not match.

source_type.description: Allowed source types (1 to 20), e.g. "Government Document", "Dataset", "Journal", "Report".

is_primary_source.description: true: primary sources only; false: non-primary only.

official_country.description: Two-letter lower-case country code, e.g. "us", for official sources of that country.

to.description: Latest year (4 digits), not before from.

domain.description: Only these domains and their subdomains (1 to 20).

exclude_domain.description: Never these domains, their subdomains or redirects into them (1 to 20).

limit.description: Maximum number of sources to return (1-20)

tools.name: get_source_preview
tools.title: Preview the source behind a citation
tools.description:
Open a citation at its quoted passage in the source, to show the evidence.

Use this when you need to:
- Show the exact passage a citation came from (not just the URL)
- Get a deep link that scrolls to the quote (web) or opens the cited PDF page
- Verify a quote is actually present in its source before relying on it

Works for two source types:
- **Web** (pass `url`): returns a text-fragment deep link (url#:~:text=quote).
- **Document** (pass `asset_id` from upload_file): returns the cited page's extracted text and an asset_url#page=N link. Spreadsheets return the sheet grid.

Every preview reports **bindBack**: whether the quote was found in the source (grounded) and how it matched (exact / normalized / unbound). A quote that cannot be bound back is never reported as grounded.

Related: verify_batch checks many quotes at once and returns a verification band per item; read_source_unit reads a stored source unit by its IDs rather than by URL, page or quote; get_citation returns a saved verification record, not the source passage.

Credits: 1

annotations.title: Preview the source behind a citation

url.description: Web source URL to preview, as cited (provide this OR asset_id).

asset_id.description: Uploaded asset ID from upload_file (provide this OR url). Also accepts an "asset://<id>" citation url.

page.description: 1-based page (PDF) or sheet index (spreadsheet), for an asset_id source. Default: 1

quote.description: The cited quote to bind back against the source and highlight. Without it the preview shows the page but cannot report the quote as grounded.

tools.name: verify_batch
tools.title: Verify several claims
tools.description:
Check that quotes appear in the sources you provide (text, URL or uploaded file), many at once. Each item is a quote plus its source: inline text, a URL, or an uploaded asset.

Per item you get back whether the quote is grounded, how it matched (exact / normalized / fuzzy / unbound), the best-matching passage and score even when unbound, a verification band, and a feedback_token.

A fuzzy match is capped at needs_review and never reported as verified.

Use this when you need to:
- Check every citation in a document at once
- Confirm quotes you (or another model) produced actually appear in their sources
- Get feedback tokens so a human can accept or reject each result

Related: verify_claim returns a verdict from web search; get_source_preview shows one quote in place with a deep link; verify_feedback records a human verdict on one of these results.

Deterministic — no model calls. Credits: 1 per item — the work is per item, so a 200-claim batch costs 200. Max 200 items per call.

items.description: The quotes to check, each against its own source (1-200 items).

id.description: Your own id, echoed back on the result so you can map it.

quote.description: The claim or quote to check.

source_text.description: The source text to check the quote against. Provide this, or url, or asset_id.

url.description: A web source URL to resolve and check against. Provide this, or source_text, or asset_id.

asset_id.description: An uploaded asset ID (from upload_file or upload_url) to check against. Provide this, or source_text, or url.

page.description: 1-based page, for an asset source. Omit to search the whole asset.

tools.name: upload_file
tools.title: Upload a file
tools.description:
Upload a PDF, scan, image, spreadsheet or office file to Webcite and get an asset_id for extraction or review.

Use this when you need to:
- Verify claims against a specific document
- Provide additional context for fact-checking
- Upload research papers or reports for analysis

Returns a file ID you can pass as asset_id to get_source_preview, extract_document, extract_figures, classify_document and analyze_document.

Related: upload_url fetches a file from a public HTTPS link instead of a local path; extract_document, extract_figures and classify_document can also read a file directly from asset_url without an upload.

Credits: 1

file_path.description: Absolute path to a local file to upload (PDF, image, spreadsheet, docx, pptx, html or txt).

tools.name: extract_document
tools.title: Extract a document to Markdown
tools.description:
Parse a PDF, scan, spreadsheet or office file to Markdown page by page (OCR included), with the page or sheet each part came from. Returns normalized text with provenance: whole-doc markdown, per-page/sheet units carrying their page or sheet, and (for spreadsheets) sheet names.

Handles PDF, spreadsheets, docx, pptx, html, txt and JPEG/PNG/WebP images. Deterministic-first; scanned PDFs and images fall back to vision OCR. Check the returned read status and issue: empty text is not proof that a document has no data.

Only the text display is truncated. Some MCP clients omit structuredContent. Keep source_version_id from upload_file; get_latest_representation and read_source_unit retrieve saved units by ID. If the IDs are unavailable, extract_pages costs 1 credit. Do not treat a truncated display as full coverage.

Extraction does not fact-check claims; whole-document or whole-slide external fact-checking is done by review_document, which reads the stored source itself.

Related: extract_pages returns chunks for RAG indexing instead of whole-document Markdown; extract_figures returns financial metrics only; analyze_document checks figures for internal conflicts.

Optional visual_rendition: true creates model-generated layout evidence for an owned JPEG/PNG and exact source_version_id. Supply an explicit idempotency_key and preserve it on uncertain recovery. Returns a partial representation and source_units IDs for read_source_unit without replacing the selected source. The dedicated visual endpoint refuses on an unsupported server; never fall back to ordinary extraction. Default extraction is unchanged. Inspect operation receipts for provider usage; a layout role is not certification.

Credits: 1

asset_id.description: An uploaded asset ID from upload_file. Provide this OR asset_url.

asset_url.description: A direct URL to the file (e.g. your own signed storage URL), so the file need not be uploaded to Webcite. Provide this OR asset_id.

mode.description: lite or standard. When mode is omitted, accounts created on or after 20 November 2026 (04:00 UTC) read in lite and older accounts read in standard. lite is the faster, lower-cost read (balance estimate 0.12 credits a page); standard is the higher-accuracy read (0.75 credits a page), better on complex tables, handwriting and scans. Either can always be sent explicitly.

visual_rendition.description: Explicit JPEG/PNG layout evidence; requires owned asset_id, source_version_id and idempotency_key.

source_version_id.description: Exact immutable owned source version, only with visual_rendition:true.

idempotency_key.description: Explicit operation identity for visual rendition. Preserve this key; never automatically redispatch under a new key.

tools.name: extract_figures
tools.title: Extract figures from a document
tools.description:
Extract financial figures from a document with units, periods and source locations. Returns recognized financial metrics as tagged, source-grounded figures: the value normalized to its canonical unit, what it means (`metric`), `unit`, optional `entity`/`period`, a confidence `band`, whether it was confirmed against the cited cell (`bound`), and full `provenance` (asset, sheet, cell, page). This is not a complete inventory of every number.

This is deterministic financial-model reading: header scale ("$M" / "'000"), accounting negatives, period columns (FY2023 vs FY2024) and unit declarations are all honoured, so a percentage is never mis-read as a currency.

Reads spreadsheets (cell-level), PDFs with a text layer (grounded and cited by page), and other text formats deterministically. Scanned pages and images go through vision OCR first, then grounding, and are marked as model reads.

The output is in the figures format analyze_conflicts accepts.

Related: analyze_document reads the figures and also checks them for conflicts and recomputations; extract_document returns all text, not only metrics.

Credits: 2

asset_id.description: An uploaded asset ID from upload_file. Provide this OR asset_url.

asset_url.description: A direct URL to the file (e.g. your own signed storage URL), so the file need not be uploaded to Webcite. Provide this OR asset_id.

tools.name: list_citations
tools.title: List saved citations
tools.description:
List your past claim verifications, with each record's ID, prompt and date. Paginated; filter by thread_id to continue one session.

Related: get_citation returns the full saved result (sources, stances, verdict) for one ID from this list; get_document_review reads saved whole-document reviews, which are not listed here.

Credits: 1

thread_id.description: Filter by thread ID to get citations from a specific session

tools.name: get_citation
tools.title: Get a saved citation
tools.description:
Get one saved claim verification by its citation ID, with its prompt, sources, stances and verdict. Reads the stored result; nothing is re-verified.

Related: list_citations finds the IDs; get_source_preview opens a cited source at its quoted passage.

Credits: 1

citation_id.description: The citation ID to retrieve, as returned by list_citations or a verification result.

tools.name: analyze_conflicts
tools.title: Check figures for conflicts

figures.description: Figures extracted across one or more documents, in the extract_figures output format.

value.description: Value normalized to the metric's canonical unit.

assetId.description: Asset ID of the source document.

documentName.description: Display name of the source document.

method.description: How the value was extracted: rule (deterministic) or model (OCR or model read).

tools.name: upload_url
tools.title: Upload a file from a URL
tools.description:
Upload a file from a public HTTPS URL to Webcite and get an asset_id for extraction or review. Stores the original file bytes, including through hosted MCP. No caller credentials or headers are forwarded. Private addresses, unsafe redirects, unsupported formats, empty files and files over 100 MB are refused. This does not access a local file or a private chat attachment. Save asset_id, asset_url and source_version_id; use the owned asset_id for review and extraction. An uncertain failure does not prove that no upload charge occurred; preserve the receipt rather than automatically repeating it.

Related: upload_file takes a local file instead of a link.

Credits: 1 for a stored upload.

annotations.title: Upload a file from a URL

url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the original file, up to 8,192 characters; at most 100 MB.

filename.description: Optional display filename, 1 to 255 characters, whose extension matches the fetched format (for example report.pdf).

tools.name: analyze_document
tools.title: Analyze figures in a document
tools.description:
Analyze figures in an uploaded PDF, spreadsheet or JPEG/PNG/WebP image. Image figures are OCR/model reads that need source review; an absent or ambiguous figure is not a verified zero. Returns figures, conflicts, recomputations, a review flag and category. Checks internal numeric consistency only; external fact-checking of every claim is done by review_document.

- **Spreadsheets** (xlsx/xls/csv): extracted deterministically with exact cell provenance. No model calls.
- **PDFs**: the page image is read for the printed figures (it never computes); those are image reads, capped at needs_review. Requires image reading to be configured on the server.
- **JPEG/PNG/WebP**: OCR reads the image, then source-grounded finance analysis checks recognized figures. Incompatible or missing arithmetic scope remains unresolved.

Related: extract_figures returns the figures without conflict checks; analyze_conflicts checks figures you supply; ask_document answers one numeric question over supplied text; review_document fact-checks claims against external sources.

Credits: 3. The document is downloaded and parsed. PDFs and images may require vision reads. Rate-limited more strictly than compute-only endpoints.

asset_id.description: The uploaded PDF, spreadsheet or JPEG/PNG/WebP asset ID from upload_file.

tools.name: classify_document
tools.title: Classify a document
tools.description:
Classify a document into a coarse **category** plus the fine multi-type **covers** it holds (a bundled workbook covers several). Deterministic and model-free — works with no model configured.

Use this when you need to:
- File an uploaded document into a data-room category
- Know what a workbook actually contains before reading it
- Produce the `category` and `covers` values that document_gaps accepts as input

Related: document_gaps lists the documents usually expected in a category; extract_document returns the text itself.

Credits: 1

asset_id.description: An uploaded asset ID from upload_file. Provide this OR asset_url.

asset_url.description: A direct URL to the file (e.g. your own signed storage URL), so the file need not be uploaded to Webcite. Provide this OR asset_id.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy preset: "vc" (venture data-room) or "ma" (M&A). Default: vc

tools.name: document_gaps
tools.title: Find gaps in a document
tools.description:
The "usually also here" checklist for a category. Given the documents already filed in it, returns each expected document type flagged present or absent. An item counts as present when any document matches it by filename, category, or covered type.

Advisory — nothing blocks. Pure and deterministic, no I/O and no model calls.

Related: classify_document produces the category and covers for one file.

Credits: 1

category.description: The category whose expected-documents checklist to compute.

docs.description: The documents currently filed in that category.

filename.description: File name, matched against expected document types.

category.description: Category this document was filed under.

covers.description: Fine types this document covers, e.g. from classify_document.

stage.description: Company stage, to tailor the checklist.

tools.name: accuracy_report
tools.title: Get the numeric accuracy report
tools.description:
The numeric engine's measured accuracy against its gold-set corpus: conflict detection rate and precision, and recompute correctness. Reproducible and checked on every build.

Returns measured figures for stating how accurate the verification is. Takes no input.

Related: these figures describe the engine behind analyze_conflicts and analyze_document; they are not a result for any of your documents.

Credits: 1

tools.name: verify_feedback
tools.title: Send feedback on a verification
tools.description:
Record a human verdict on a verify_batch result. Pass the feedback_token from that result plus your verdict; the token carries the result summary, so token + verdict is enough.

Feedback is stored, so corrections accumulate over time.

Related: verify_batch produces the feedback_token. A result from verify_claim or review_document carries no feedback_token.

Credits: 1

token.description: The feedback_token returned by verify_batch for the result being judged.

note.description: Optional note or correction explaining the verdict.

tools.name: verify_claim_stream
tools.title: Verify a claim with streamed progress
tools.description:
Fact-check one claim through the streaming endpoint: returns the same citations, stances and verdict as verify_claim plus the intermediate stream events. The events (sub-claim decomposition progress, per-sub-claim results) are collected while the request runs and returned with the final result as stream_events; they are not pushed to the client as live progress.

Suited to:
- Complex or multi-part claims that may take a long time to verify
- Cases that need the intermediate data (sub-claim decomposition, per-sub-claim results)
- Long-running verifications where a single HTTP request could time out

Related: verify_claim gives the same result without the event log and accepts an idempotency_key for safe retries; verify_batch checks quotes against sources you supply.

Output format and credits match verify_claim (2-4 credits).

annotations.title: Verify a claim with streamed progress

claim.description: The factual claim to verify (e.g., "Japan's population fell below 120 million in 2025")

source_urls.description: Up to five public HTTPS source URLs, including readable PDFs, to read directly. Pass user-provided official reports here rather than relying on search.

filters.description: Optional source constraints. A source whose required metadata is unknown does not match.

source_type.description: Allowed source types (1 to 20), e.g. "Government Document", "Dataset", "Journal", "Report".

is_primary_source.description: true: primary sources only; false: non-primary only.

official_country.description: Two-letter lower-case country code, e.g. "us", for official sources of that country.

to.description: Latest year (4 digits), not before from.

domain.description: Only these domains and their subdomains (1 to 20).

exclude_domain.description: Never these domains, their subdomains or redirects into them (1 to 20).

thread_id.description: Thread ID to group related verifications in a session. Pass the same thread_id to continue a conversation.

include_stance.description: Include stance analysis (supports/contradicts) for each source. Adds 1 credit. Default: true

include_verdict.description: Generate an overall verdict with confidence score. Adds 1 credit. Default: true

decompose_claim.description: Break complex claims into sub-claims and verify each independently; the sub-claim results appear in stream_events.

tools.name: ask_document
tools.title: Ask a numeric question about a document
tools.description: Answer one numeric question from document text you supply, with each number checked against that text. Starts a job and returns a job ID; the result is read with get_ask_result. It does not search for external source URLs or identify the original publisher. Costs 5 credits. Unverified numbers remain null. Related: verify_claim checks a claim against web sources; analyze_document checks figures in an uploaded file; extract_figures lists recognized metrics.

annotations.title: Ask a numeric question about a document

question.description: The numeric question to answer from the document, 1 to 2,000 characters.

documentText.description: The document text to answer from (for example extract_document Markdown), up to 2,000,000 characters.

documentName.description: Optional label for the document, up to 300 characters.

hasTextLayer.description: Set false when the source is a scan with no text layer, so an empty read is reported as needing OCR.

topK.description: Retrieved passages used to draft the answer, 1 to 20 (server default 8).

tools.name: extract_pages
tools.title: Extract selected pages
tools.description: Split an uploaded document into citation-ready chunks with page, sheet or section anchors, for RAG indexing. Returns the chunks, plus extraction state and reason even when no chunks exist. An asset you do not own returns not_found (Asset not found). Related: extract_document returns whole-document Markdown with per-page units for reading; extract_figures returns financial metrics. Costs 1 credit.

asset_id.description: An uploaded asset ID from upload_file. Provide this OR asset_url.

asset_url.description: A direct URL to the file (e.g. your own signed storage URL), so the file need not be uploaded to Webcite. Provide this OR asset_id.

mode.description: lite or standard. When mode is omitted, accounts created on or after 20 November 2026 (04:00 UTC) read in lite and older accounts read in standard. lite is the faster, lower-cost read (balance estimate 0.12 credits a page); standard is the higher-accuracy read (0.75 credits a page), better on complex tables, handwriting and scans. Either can always be sent explicitly.

tools.name: get_ask_result
tools.title: Get a document answer
tools.description: Read the status and answer of an ask_document job by its job ID. Returns queued, running, done or failed status and the checked result when ready; a failed job carries an error code and message. An unknown job or one you do not own returns not_found. Costs 0 credits. Related: get_document_review_job reports document review jobs, not ask_document jobs.

tools.name: get_document_review
tools.title: Get a saved document review
tools.description: Read a document review: claims, verdicts, citations and passages not covered. Reads the saved review by review_id without new analysis or credits. Page claims, uncovered passages, rejected candidates and explicit reviewer dispositions independently. The API key must own the review; an unknown review or one you do not own returns not_found. Related: get_document_review_job reports job status and progress, not results; review_document starts a review; get_citation reads a single-claim verification.

review_id.description: Saved review ID, as returned by review_document or get_document_review_job.

limit.description: Claims per page, 1 to 100 (default 50). Continue with next_offset until all claims are read.

gap_limit.description: Uncovered passages per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Continue with next_gap_offset.

rejected_limit.description: Rejected claim candidates per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Continue with next_rejected_offset.

disposition_limit.description: Explicit nonclaim dispositions per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Continue with next_disposition_offset.

tools.name: get_document_review_job
tools.title: Get document review progress
tools.description: Check progress of a document review job. Reads the durable job by job_id at zero credits. Queued, running, waiting_parse and waiting_review are nonterminal. Terminal statuses are complete, partial_coverage, credits_exhausted and failed. Returns the job status, progress and review_id; saved claims and uncovered source spans are read by review_id with get_document_review. Related: review_document starts or resumes the job; get_ask_result reports an ask_document job, not a review.

job_id.description: Review job ID returned by review_document: a 36-character UUID or 64 hex characters.

tools.name: get_latest_representation
tools.title: Get the latest source representation
tools.description: Locate the latest representation and source unit IDs of an owned retained source. These IDs address source units for evidence reads and numeric verification. ID chain: upload_file, upload_url or register_source returns source_version_id; it returns its representationId and each unit's sourceUnitId, locator and state (units sorted by unit key, so page:10 precedes page:2; at most 2,000; no content). "Latest" does not mean "newest": it succeeds only when the version has exactly one representation (or one selected analysis); with two or more it returns api_error 409 Representation selection required, and with none not_found. A missing, unavailable or other account's source version returns not_found (Source version unavailable); an asset you do not own returns unauthorized (Source access denied). Returns IDs only; read_source_unit returns a unit's text, and get_source_preview shows a cited passage. Related: publish_text_representation creates a representation when none exists.

source_version_id.description: Owned retained source version ID, as returned by upload_file, upload_url or register_source.

tools.name: get_review_source_span
tools.title: Get an unchecked review source span
tools.description: Read the exact text of one owned saved uncovered source passage for review, including an inactive failed residual review. A role may be unknown; this read does not establish structural or nonclaim proof. asset_id, start and end must exactly match one uncovered_source_spans entry that get_document_review lists for that review. Offsets are 0-based character positions (UTF-16) into the review's stored source, end exclusive, at most 16,000 apart. A span that is not a saved gap, or an asset outside that review, returns api_error 400; a running review or changed source returns api_error 409; an unknown review or one you do not own returns not_found. Related: get_document_review lists the uncovered passages and their offsets; record_review_nonclaim records a nonclaim assessment for the passage. Costs 0 credits.

annotations.title: Get an unchecked review source span

review_id.description: Saved review ID that holds the uncovered passage.

asset_id.description: Asset ID (UUID) of the reviewed source, as listed with the uncovered passage.

start.description: Start character offset of the saved uncovered passage, exactly as listed.

end.description: End character offset (exclusive), exactly as listed; the passage is at most 16,000 characters.

tools.name: prepare_ocr_rescue
tools.title: Prepare an OCR rescue
tools.description: Prepare judged OCR rescue for an owned OCR source representation before previewing unresolved citations. A new successful preparation costs 5 credits; retained replays cost 0 credits. Requires the backend OCR feature; return unavailable states honestly. representation_id must be a representation of source_version_id (from get_latest_representation), otherwise not_found. Returns either attempted false with code disabled or not_ocr, or prepared, calibrationKey, candidateCount and decidedAt. Related: get_source_preview previews citations; extract_document is the ordinary extraction, with OCR fallback.

representation_id.description: ID of the OCR source representation to prepare.

tools.name: publish_text_representation
tools.title: Publish a text representation
tools.description: Publish a deterministic text or CSV representation of an owned retained source. Returns representation and source unit IDs for verify_numeric_claim, shaped like the get_latest_representation result. Accepts plain or CSV sources of at most 1 MiB of UTF-8; form feeds split pages, at most 2,000 units; other sources return api_error 400. Repeating the call returns the same representation. A missing, unavailable or other account's source version returns not_found (Source version unavailable); an asset you do not own returns unauthorized (Source access denied). Related: get_latest_representation looks up an existing representation without creating one. No model call.

source_version_id.description: Owned retained source version ID, as returned by register_source.

tools.name: read_source_unit
tools.title: Read a source unit
tools.description: Read one owned immutable source unit by the IDs returned from a source representation. All three IDs must come from one chain: source_version_id from upload_file, upload_url or register_source, and representation_id and source_unit_id from the same get_latest_representation or publish_text_representation result (or a visual rendition). If the unit does not belong to that representation, or the representation belongs to another version, the result is not_found (anchor_unresolved). A missing, unavailable or other account's source version returns not_found (Source version unavailable); an asset you do not own returns unauthorized (Source access denied). Returns its text and numeric content, which identify the figure_index values for numeric verification. Related: get_latest_representation lists the unit IDs; get_source_preview opens a page or URL by quote instead of by unit ID.

representation_id.description: Representation ID from get_latest_representation, publish_text_representation or a visual rendition.

source_unit_id.description: Source unit ID within that representation.

tools.name: record_review_nonclaim
tools.title: Mark a review span as not a claim
tools.description: Record an explicit assessment that an exact source-attested heading, table title or navigation passage contains no factual assertion. The assessment must cover the full passage text (get_review_source_span returns it); a structural role alone never proves nonclaim. Optional visual_evidence references stored model layout for the same immutable source; the server rechecks literal offsets and geometry. An isolated page footer can qualify, factual/numeric headings cannot. Agent actions are not analyst approval. Failed residual-only reviews may reconcile retained complete extraction responses without new generation; missing evidence refuses. Leave assertion-bearing passages uncovered and source partial. Records rationale and authenticated reviewer identity. review_id, asset_id, start and end must match one saved uncovered span exactly, as for get_review_source_span; otherwise api_error 400. Related: get_review_source_span reads the passage without recording anything. Costs 0 credits.

annotations.title: Mark a review span as not a claim

review_id.description: Saved review ID that holds the uncovered passage.

asset_id.description: Asset ID (UUID) of the reviewed source.

start.description: Start character offset of the saved uncovered passage, exactly as listed.

end.description: End character offset (exclusive), exactly as listed.

source_quote.description: The full passage text exactly as get_review_source_span returned it; its length must equal end minus start (at most 16,000 characters).

rationale.description: Why the whole passage contains no factual assertion, 10 to 1,000 characters.

visual_evidence.description: Optional reference to stored visual layout evidence for the same source; only these two fields are accepted.

representation_id.description: Visual representation ID returned by extract_document with visual_rendition, up to 191 characters.

unit_key.description: Visual unit key in the form visual-page:<n>:element:<n>.

tools.name: register_source
tools.title: Register a retained source
tools.description: Register original text or CSV bytes for an uploaded, owned asset. Returns a retained sourceVersionId and the assetId for source representation and numeric verification. The bytes are not compared with the asset's existing content: they become a new retained version and the asset's selected version, and identical bytes return the earlier version. An asset you do not own returns unauthorized (Source access denied). Related: upload_file and upload_url create the asset; publish_text_representation turns the registered version into readable units.

asset_id.description: Owned asset ID to attach the original bytes to.

filename.description: File name with an extension matching the bytes (for example data.csv), up to 255 characters.

file_base64.description: Base64-encoded original file bytes, 1 byte to 20 MB decoded.

tools.name: review_document
tools.title: Fact-check a whole document
tools.description: Fact-check every material claim in an uploaded document and report coverage; starts a job and returns a job_id. Fits requests such as "audit this document" or "check every figure on this slide". Input: the existing asset_id(s), a prompt and a stable thread_id. The server parses the stored source itself, so no separate extraction step is needed. Unlike separate single-claim checks, it covers every claim and saves progress. Starts a durable full review and immediately returns a job_id; job status comes from get_document_review_job and saved result pages from get_document_review. Repeating the same input reuses its job without a new charge. A failed or credit-exhausted review resumes on the same thread and exact inputs with retry_failed: true and the returned retry_idempotency_key (or the original key); completed claims and the failed job receipt are preserved. Full coverage is reported only when coverage_complete is true. Related: verify_claim covers a single claim; extract_document only parses; analyze_document stays within the numbers of the file.

prompt.description: What to verify in the uploaded document.

asset_ids.description: One or more distinct uploaded asset IDs (from upload_file or upload_url) to review together.

thread_id.description: Stable ID for this review. Reuse the same value and exact inputs to resume.

review_scope.description: Whole-document scope. This tool always requests full coverage; keep this value in resume_input.

source_urls.description: Official HTTPS reports supplied by the user or found with search_sources, including PDFs, that each claim must be checked against.

filters.description: Optional source constraints. A source whose required metadata is unknown does not match.

source_type.description: Allowed source types (1 to 20), e.g. "Government Document", "Dataset", "Journal", "Report".

is_primary_source.description: true: primary sources only; false: non-primary only.

official_country.description: Two-letter lower-case country code, e.g. "us", for official sources of that country.

to.description: Latest year (4 digits), not before from.

domain.description: Only these domains and their subdomains (1 to 20).

exclude_domain.description: Never these domains, their subdomains or redirects into them (1 to 20).

include_stance.description: Analyze source stance; adds 1 credit per claim.

include_verdict.description: Generate a verdict; adds 1 credit per claim.

max_account_credits.description: Optional cap on new account-credit charges and outstanding holds for this execution, including a retry execution. Completed results replay without charge. Immutable for the same job/idempotency key; changing or omitting an existing cap conflicts. Does not cap provider cost or calls. Omission requests no execution cap.

retry_failed.description: Explicitly resume a diagnosed failed review on the same thread and inputs. Preserve the original idempotency key, or use the returned retry_idempotency_key. Completed claims and extraction responses are reused; the failed job receipt is retained.

idempotency_key.description: Omit on first start. For retry_failed: true, reuse the original key or the returned retry_idempotency_key with exactly the same inputs.

tools.name: revise_document_claim_analysis
tools.title: Revise a reviewed claim analysis
tools.description: Re-evaluate one owned, settled saved claim using retained snippets and the current evidence policy, without new research, model calls or credits. The review must be inactive. Requires original_result_hash, as returned for the claim by get_document_review. Idempotent for the original result and policy version. Preserves the original result and credit receipt; missing scope assessment remains inconclusive. claim_id must be a claim of review_id: a claim outside the review returns api_error 409 Saved claim analysis not found, a different hash 409 Original analysis changed, an active review 409, and an unknown review or one you do not own not_found. Related: review_document with retry_failed resumes unfinished claims with new research; verify_claim checks a claim afresh.

review_id.description: Saved review ID; the review must be inactive.

claim_id.description: Saved claim ID within that review, as returned by get_document_review.

original_result_hash.description: The claim's original_result_hash from get_document_review: 64 lower-case hex characters.

tools.name: verify_numeric_claim
tools.title: Check arithmetic in a claim
tools.description: Assess arithmetic against one or two retained figures from owned source units. This is arithmetic scope, not full semantic verification. Each operand's three IDs must belong together as for read_source_unit, or the result is not_found; figure_index is 0-based over the values within the unit's first 20,000 characters (CSV year columns skipped); an out-of-range or ambiguous index returns api_error 400. Returns outcome supported, contradicted, escalate or not_applicable, with scope arithmetic_only. Related: verify_claim checks a claim against web sources; analyze_conflicts recomputes metrics across many supplied figures.

claim.description: The sentence whose arithmetic to check, 1 to 10,000 characters.

operands.description: One or two retained figures the claim relies on.

source_unit_id.description: Source unit ID holding the figure.

figure_index.description: 0-based index of the figure within that unit's numeric content, as read with read_source_unit.
